Data freshness and the limits of a signal

Why the app waits, how monitoring works, and what the analysis cannot tell you.

Contract Compass guide · Updated November 6, 2026

Contract Compass combines completed-candle analysis with a live reference price. Those inputs arrive through separate public market feeds, so a visible chart and a connected price feed do not by themselves prove that an entry is current.

Completed candles and live prices have different jobs

The chart uses candles that have closed. A candle still forming can change shape and volume before it closes. The app does not let an unfinished candle independently confirm an entry.

The live mark price then checks whether that earlier setup is still usable under the app’s rules. A price that has lost the breakout, moved through the stop, reached the first target, or become extended can remove the entry signal.

Freshness is a safety condition

A quote more than 10 seconds old or an analysis more than 90 seconds old cannot support a new entry here. These limits are rules chosen for this app, not promises that younger data is accurate or profitable. An unavailable state tells you to restore current information before using an entry.

Completed-candle analysis normally refreshes every 60 seconds and after a candle-close notification. When a new closed candle is detected, the app suppresses the older entry until its analysis catches up. If a feed disconnects, it attempts to reconnect with a bounded delay.

Monitoring needs an open, visible page

Switching away from the browser tab pauses monitoring. Returning requests fresh information before resuming. Closing the page ends monitoring: there is no background alert service, text-message notification, or promise of an alert after the app closes.

The activity list records changes seen during the current page session. It is not a verified history of trades, backtest, profit record, or evidence that every signal was captured.

The rules do not predict the future

The app combines trend averages, breakout levels, momentum, volume, and estimated reward relative to risk. These calculations summarize selected price history. They do not read breaking news, order-book depth, exchange outages, or your portfolio. A market regime can change after all checks agree.

No trained prediction model or validated win rate is claimed. The target prices are conditional projections. The app cannot promise an execution price, the order in which stop and target will be reached, or any particular return.

Check the source and the assumptions

The interface identifies its contract, candle interval, holding horizon, analysis time, and monitoring status. Use those labels when reporting an issue. Do not send private exchange information to reproduce a public-data problem.

Market connections follow the Binance USDⓈ-M market-stream documentation. The exact app rules can be inspected in the public source repository. For what the calculator includes, see Understand the risk calculator.
